bottom_line: Atmospheric water generation can provide drinking water for emergency, remote, military, disaster, or humid-site uses. Current condensing systems are not credible replacements for ordinary U.S. household or community utility volumes because output falls in cool/dry air, electricity requirements scale steeply, and condensate needs potable-water treatment and maintenance.

limits: rated output often measured under favorable conditions

strengths: can use thermal or solar regeneration
low operating energy in favorable microclimates

water_quality.finding: Condensate is not inherently sterile or automatically potable. Air contaminants, wetted surfaces, storage, biofilms, and maintenance create chemical and microbial risks.
water_quality.observations: EPA field work found heterotrophic bacteria and evidence of opportunistic pathogens in real-world systems.
